title: Bioengineering microfluidic organoids-on-a-chip
protocol: Prepare base medium (BM) by supplementing Advanced DMEM/F12 medium with 1x Glutamax, 10 mM HEPES, and 100 μg/ml Penicillin/Streptomycin.
Store BM at +4°C for up to 1 month.
Prepare base medium with growth factors (BMGF) by supplementing BM with 1x B27 supplement, 1x N2 supplement, and 1 mM N-acetylcysteine.
Store BMGF at +4°C for up to 2 weeks.
Prepare ISC expansion medium (ENRCV) by supplementing BMGF with growth factors: 50 ng/ml EGF, 100 ng/ml Noggin, 500 ng/ml R-Spondin 1, 3 μM CHIR99021, and 1 mM valproic acid.
For freshly extracted mouse crypts and single-cell culture, add 2.5 μM Thiazovivin to ENRCV medium for the first two days.
Thaw Matrigel on ice for 30 minutes in advance.
Place a new 24-well plate into the incubator at 37°C for preheating.
Take 2 ml of BM and keep it on ice for each well to be split.
Aspirate the medium from wells containing organoids embedded in Matrigel.
Add 950 µl of BM to the well and disrupt Matrigel drops by pipetting up and down several times.
Collect the well contents in a 15 ml tube on ice.
Spin down at 800 rpm for 3 minutes at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and resuspend organoids in approximately 2 ml of BM. Triturate vigorously with a glass pipette for 15-20 times.
Spin down at 900 rpm for 4 minutes at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and resuspend organoids in Matrigel. Keep the tube on ice.
Take a pre-heated 24-well plate from the incubator.
Make approximately 20-25 µl drops in each well.
Turn the plate upside down and incubate for 10-20 minutes in the incubator.
In the meantime, prepare ENRCV medium.
Add 500 µl of prewarmed ENRCV to each well.
Place the plate back into the incubator (37°C, 5% CO₂).
On the second day after passaging, replenish the ENRCV medium in each well.
On the fourth day after passaging, use the organoids for mini-gut preparation or perform another passaging step.
Wash the microdevices with ddH2O and aspirate the water from all reservoirs using a vacuum pump.
Dry the chips completely, leaving them open.
Place the chips on ice to cool down immediately before use.
Prepare hydrogel components in two cooled 1.5 ml tubes as follows:
Add 20 µl of Matrigel to Tube #1.
In Tube #2, add 10 µl of 10x DMEM, 9 µl Base medium (BM), and 1 µl 1M Sodium Bicarbonate (S).
Mix well by pipetting in Tube #2.
Add 80 µl of collagen to the tube containing the Matrigel solution, mix well by pipetting.
Transfer 80 µl from Tube #1 to Tube #2, mix well by pipetting.
Mix the hydrogel very fast and carefully to prevent bubbles.
Return everything back on ice as soon as possible.
Cool down the microdevices by placing them on ice.
Dry the microdevices using a vacuum pump, ensuring no condensate remains in the matrix chamber.
Introduce 8 μl of premixed hydrogel precursor to the central matrix chamber through the hydrogel-loading port, avoiding air bubbles and ensuring contact with the row of pillars without overflowing.
Place the microdevice in a humidified 37°C incubator for 2 minutes immediately after loading the hydrogel.
Take the microdevice out of the incubator and introduce BM to the inlet and outlet medium reservoirs.
Return the microdevice to the humidified 37°C incubator for final hydrogel polymerization (30 minutes).
Fill the inlet, outlet, and basal side medium reservoirs completely with BM. Add 700 μl of PBS to the dishes around the PDMS microdevice.
Launch the PALM MicroBeam microscope and PALM Robo user interface according to the system setup guidelines.
Import the desired pattern file and move the stage to the position of the pattern on the screen.
Clean the glass bottom of the microdevice and position it on the microscope’s plate holder, in the field of view of the objective, and align with the pattern.
Carefully adjust the microdevice relative angle to make sure it is well aligned with the pattern.
Focus 160 μm above from the microdevice dish glass bottom.
Adjust settings of the laser energy and cutting speed according to your system setup, so as to achieve 120 µm-height microchannel.
Select all elements of the pattern and start laser ablation.
Inspect microdevices under the benchtop microscope: the microchannels should have a clear inner surface and sharp outlines.
Perfuse the resulting microchannels with BM. Flow of medium through the microchannel from the inlet to the outlet reservoir indicates successful laser ablation.
Remove the media from the outlet and add fresh BM to the inlet, outlet and basal side medium reservoirs.
Check regularly that there is sufficient amount of media in all reservoirs and PBS around the PDMS microdevice.
For mini-gut preparation use mouse intestinal organoids between passages 5 and 20.
Prepare dissociation solution composed of 50 μl DNAse I aliquot, 950 μl TrypLE Express solution, 1 mM N-acetylcysteine, and 10 μM Y27632.
Aspirate the medium from wells containing organoids embedded in Matrigel.
Add 950 µl of BM to the well and disrupt Matrigel drops by pipetting up and down several times.
Collect the well contents in a 15 ml tube and spin down at 800 rpm for 3 minutes at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and gently resuspend organoids in 1 ml of dissociation solution.
Dissociate organoids for 10 min at 37°C by placing the tube in the water bath. Half-way through, knock the tube to break down cell aggregates.
Prepare 10% FBS in BM, a 50-ml tube with a 40-µm cell strainer, and an empty 1.5 ml tube for single-cell suspension collection. Keep everything on ice.
After 10-min incubation, add 9 ml of 10% FBS to block the digestion.
Carefully and slowly pass the digested organoids through the 40-µm strainer.
Transfer the single cell suspension into a new 15 ml falcon and spin down at 1100 rpm for 4 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend cells in 100-200 µl of ENRCV containing 2.5 µM Thiazovivin (termed ENRCVT).
Spin down the cell suspension in a 1.5 ml tube at 1000 rpm for 3 minutes.
Resuspend the cell pellet in ENRCVT at a density of about 10^6 cells/ml.
Aspirate all media from the microchannel inlet/outlet and basal side medium reservoirs.
Introduce 10 μl of concentrated cell suspension into the laser-ablated microchannel through the inlet reservoir.
Allow cells to fill the microchannel by gravity-driven flow.
Observe under a benchtop microscope as crypt-shaped cavities fill up with cells.
Wait for about 1-2 minutes to allow cells to settle down in the crypt-shaped cavities.
Pipette up and down the single cell suspension in the inlet/outlet reservoirs to prevent sedimentation on the bottom.
Gently harvest remaining single cell suspension once crypt-shaped cavities are filled to about 50-75%.
Perfuse microdevices thoroughly with fresh ENRCVT medium to remove non-adherent cells.
Add 10 µl of ENRCVT medium to the inlet reservoir.
Remove flow-through medium from the outlet reservoir.
Wait until gravity-driven flow fills the outlet reservoir with medium again.
Repeat the process by adding more medium and removing flow-through as necessary.
Inspect microdevices under benchtop microscope to ensure crypt-shaped cavities are packed with cells, while lumen of microchannel and inlet/outlet reservoirs are devoid of cells.
Fill inlet/outlet and basal side medium reservoirs with ENRCVT medium.
Place microdevices in incubator for 48 hours.
Replenish the medium (ENRCV) in basal side reservoirs after 48 h of cell seeding.
Perfuse mini-guts after replenishing medium.
Observe on benchtop microscope to check epithelialization process, where cells should form an epithelial monolayer around crypts by the second day.
Replace ENRCV medium with differentiation medium (ENR) in the inlet/outlet reservoirs after epithelial tube formation.
Replenish the medium in the basal side reservoirs every day during tissue maturation.
Perfuse mini-guts at least once a day to remove accumulated shed epithelial cells from the lumen.
Gradually decrease the concentration of CV in the basal side media reservoirs over three days until complete removal.
Continue replenishing the medium in the basal side reservoirs every 24 hours.
